rapport_notes: Warm, professional tone throughout; good acknowledgment of customer concerns; natural conversational flow with appropriate humor.
process_discipline_notes: On-Time Guarantee mentioned twice—once in Stage 1 opening pitch ("we do have our on time guarantee") and implicitly referenced again in Stage 3 pricing discussion ("time starts as soon as we get on site"). Not a hard repeat of the exact differentiator language, but the concept appears across stages.

evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: "Do you have a few moments to go over that?" — ask present, but no explicit time-box or promise of accurate quote in return.
evidence_quotes.agenda: "Do you have any questions or concerns specifically that you would like answered on this call?" — asked after confirming contact info but before probing logistics begins. Customer responds: "We're mostly just looking for prices right now."
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raises price concern only; rep acknowledges with "Perfect" and pivots immediately to differentiators without probing what specifically about pricing matters (budget, flexibility, comparison shopping, etc.). No second-layer follow-up.
evidence_quotes.sheet1_careful_with: "We do have our no worries damage coverage. Which is our free evaluation coverage included in our hourly rate, and that provides up to $2,000 per move to repair, replace or reimburse for accidental damages." — Delivered in Stage 1 opening pitch, not as a direct answer to a damage concern the customer raised.
evidence_quotes.sheet2_whos_coming: "Our movers are not daily contracted workers. They are the most well vetted and professionally trained movers. A few days before the move. You'll get a meet mover email introducing them to you helping ease attention of strangers arriving at your front door." — Delivered in Stage 1 opening pitch, not as a direct answer to a customer concern.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee: "We do have our on time guarantee we value your time. So, if we can't make it in the time window that we arrange we start discounting money of your final bill." — Delivered in Stage 1.
evidence_quotes.communication: Not covered anywhere in the call. No mention of day-before call, named crew lead, or inbox updates.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: "A typical move your size would take two movers, one truck between six to eight hours since you are moving a two bedroom equivalent out of the one story house with everything in the garage with about a half hour drive to the third floor with stair access. I would actually book to estimate your move to take between five and a half and six and a half hours." — Range provided and personalized to specific factors.
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass_window: "Obviously, their number of factors involved in determining move time and the most important one is how well prepared you are when we get there... you only pay for the time that you use us."
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass_beats_it: "As long as we can keep the time down in our efficiency up. The last time we take the less menu end up spending at the end of the day." — Implies 15-minute increments and pay-less logic, though not explicitly stated as clearly as the rubric line.
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass_self_prep: "It seems like everything's in the garage so you can't really get more prepared than you are." — Acknowledgment, but not the proactive self-prep tip phrasing.
evidence_quotes.close: "I can get you on the schedule for today... If you would like to book you can call us or you can respond to the questions in the email that I'm sending you and we can get you on the books for that date." — Asks customer to take action but does not lock rate or ask directly for the move.

top_strength: Rep delivered all Stage 1 differentiators (damage coverage, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee) clearly and confidently, and built a complete, personalized estimate anchored to specific move factors (stair access, garage location, drive time).
coaching_note: Never ask the agenda question and then immediately pitch differentiators without exploring what the customer actually said—probe why price is the concern, and hold silence after questions like 'does that make sense' instead of filling every gap; also always deliver the Communication differentiator (day-before call, named crew lead, inbox updates) as part of the takeaway, and close with an explicit ask backed by a rate-lock.
